slot.brief: Compare the rms speeds of two gases at the same temperature given their molar masses; ask for the ratio (simple scaling).

stem: The root mean square (rms) speeds of oxygen gas (molar mass 32 g mol^-1) and hydrogen gas (molar mass 2 g mol^-1) at the same temperature are v_O2 and v_H2 respectively. What is the ratio v_O2 : v_H2?

verdicts.working: At the same temperature, rms speed is proportional to 1/√M. Thus v_O2/v_H2 = √(2/32) = 1/4.

working:
v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M), so v_O2/v_H2 = sqrt(M_H2/M_O2) = sqrt(2/32) = sqrt(1/16) = 1/4.

Independent check: At the same temperature, rms speed is proportional to 1/√M. Thus v_O2/v_H2 = √(2/32) = 1/4.
solution: At the same temperature, $v_{\rm rms}=\sqrt{3RT/M}$, so $v_{O_2}/v_{H_2}=\sqrt{M_{H_2}/M_{O_2}}$. $$\frac{v_{O_2}}{v_{H_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{32}}=\frac14$$ Hence, $v_{O_2}:v_{H_2}=1:4$.
